## Key Findings

  + The number of live births in US Territories increased from `r year.rate20_24[2, 3]` births in 2020 to `r year.rate20_24[6, 3]` births in 2024.  
  
  + The preterm birth rate was `r year.rate20_24[6,4]` preterm births per 100 live births in 2024, up from `r year.rate20_24[6,4]` preterm births per 100 live births in 2020.
  
  + Mothers ages `r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MAGER.recode") %>% slice_max(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(Value)` had the highest preterm birth rate during 2020-2024 (`r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MAGER.recode") %>% slice_max(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(preterm_rate_per100)` per 100 live births), while mothers ages `r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MAGER.recode") %>% slice_min(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(Value)` had the lowest preterm birth rate during 2020-2024 (`r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MAGER.recode") %>% slice_min(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(preterm_rate_per100)` per 100 live births).
  
  + Mothers reported to be of `r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MRACEHISP.fact") %>% slice_max(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(Value)` race and ethnicity had the highest preterm birth rate during 2020-2024 (`r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MRACEHISP.fact") %>% slice_max(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(preterm_rate_per100)` per 100 live births), while mothers reported to be of `r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MRACEHISP.fact") %>% slice_min(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(Value)` race and ethnicity had the lowest preterm birth rate during 2020-2024 (`r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MRACEHISP.fact") %>% slice_min(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(preterm_rate_per100)` per 100 live births). 
  
  + The preterm birth rate was higher for mothers with any diabetes and any hypertension, with a rate `r hype.diab.rates %>% filter(Comorbidity == "DIAB.recode") %>% summarise(round(preterm_rate_per100[Reported == "Yes"]/preterm_rate_per100[Reported == "No"], 1)) %>% pull()` and `r hype.diab.rates %>% filter(Comorbidity == "HYPE.recode") %>% summarise(round(preterm_rate_per100[Reported == "Yes"]/preterm_rate_per100[Reported == "No"], 1)) %>% pull()` times the rate for no diabetes and no hypertension, respectively. 
    

## The number of births increased from 2020 to 2024

The number of live births in US Territories increased from `r year.rate20_24[2, 3]` births in 2020 to `r year.rate20_24[6, 3]` births in 2024.

```{r, echo = F}
# Start by renaming our preterm birth rate variable to `Preterm Birth Rate Per 100 Live Births`
# Show the output from each line

year.rate20_24 %>%
  rename("Preterm Births per 100 Live Births" = "preterm_rate_per100") %>%
  flextable() %>%
  theme_vanilla() %>%               # Applies a clean theme
  bg(i = 1, bg = "#5B3DB2", part = "header") %>% # Background color for header
  color(i = 1, color = "white", part = "header") %>%
  bold(j = ~ `Birth Year`) %>%             # Bold a specific column
  set_caption(caption = "Table 1: Preterm Birth Rates by Year") %>%
  width(j = c("Birth Year", "Preterm Births", "Live Births", "Preterm Births per 100 Live Births"),
        width = c(1.5, 1.2, 1.2, 2)) %>%
  ### TRY ON YOUR OWN!!!
  ## try on your own! center the columns
  align(align = "center", part = "all")
  
## take a minute to play around with some of the flextable options

## https://ardata-fr.github.io/flextable-book/static/pdf/cheat_sheet_flextable.pdf

```


## The preterm birth rate increased during 2020 to 2024

The preterm birth rate was `r year.rate20_24[6,4]` preterm births per 100 live births in 2024, up from `r year.rate20_24[2,4]` preterm births per 100 live births in 2020.

The 5-year preterm birth rate for 2020-2024 was `r year.rate20_24[6,1]` preterm births per 100 live births.

```{r fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, dpi=500, include = F}
# Start with this
year.rate20_24 %>%
  filter(`Birth Year` != "Overall 2020-2024") %>%
  mutate(`Birth Year` = as.numeric(`Birth Year`)) %>% # ggplot2 wants year to be ordered 
  ggplot(aes(x = `Birth Year`, y = `preterm_rate_per100`)) +
          geom_line(size = 1.5, color = "steelblue") +
          geom_point(size = 3, color = "black") +
          labs(
            title = "Figure 1. Preterm Birth Rate per 100 Live Births, U.S. Territories, 2020-2024",
            x = "Year",
            y = "Preterm Birth Rate per 100"
          ) +
          theme_minimal()

# Clean Up: remove X title (year is obvious, add limits on the y axis to bring to scale,
# change dot and line colors to match, bold x and y axis tick numbers)
plot2 <- year.rate20_24 %>%
  filter(`Birth Year` != "Overall 2020-2024") %>%
  mutate(`Birth Year` = as.numeric(`Birth Year`)) %>% # ggplot2 wants year to be ordered 
  ggplot(aes(x = `Birth Year`, y = `preterm_rate_per100`)) +
          geom_line(size = 1.5, color = "black") +
          geom_point(size = 3, color = "black") +
          labs(
            title = "Figure 1. Preterm Birth Rate per 100 Live Births, U.S. Territories, 2020-2024",
            x = NULL,
            y = "Rate per 100 Live Births"
          ) +
          theme_minimal() +
          ylim(0, 15) + # change y-axis limits to range from 0 to 15
          theme(
            axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
            axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13)
          )

plot2
```

```{r fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, dpi=500, echo = F, warning = F}
### What if we want to highlight the 2024 point with different color & text?
plot2 +
  geom_point(
    data = year.rate20_24 %>% filter(`Birth Year` == "2024"),
    aes(as.numeric(`Birth Year`), preterm_rate_per100),
    color = "#5B3DB2",
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = year.rate20_24 %>% filter(`Birth Year` == "2024"),
    aes(as.numeric(`Birth Year`), preterm_rate_per100, label = preterm_rate_per100),
    vjust = -1,
    color = "#5B3DB2",
    fontface = "bold"
  )

```

## Preterm birth rates varied by maternal age and maternal race and ethnicity

Mothers ages `r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MAGER.recode") %>% slice_max(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(Value)` had the highest preterm birth rate during 2020-2024 (`r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MAGER.recode") %>% slice_max(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(preterm_rate_per100)` per 100 live births), while mothers ages `r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MAGER.recode") %>% slice_min(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(Value)` had the lowest preterm birth rate during 2020-2024 (`r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MAGER.recode") %>% slice_min(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(preterm_rate_per100)` per 100 live births).

Mothers reported to be of `r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MRACEHISP.fact") %>% slice_max(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(Value)` race and ethnicity had the highest preterm birth rate during 2020-2024 (`r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MRACEHISP.fact") %>% slice_max(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(preterm_rate_per100)` per 100 live births), while mothers reported to be of `r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MRACEHISP.fact") %>% slice_min(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(Value)` race and ethnicity had the lowest preterm birth rate during 2020-2024 (`r age.raceeth.rates %>% filter(Variable == "MRACEHISP.fact") %>% slice_min(preterm_rate_per100) %>% pull(preterm_rate_per100)` per 100 live births). 

```{r include = F}
# starting just with one variable (maternal age)
age.raceeth.rates %>%
      filter(Variable == "MAGER.recode") %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = Value, y = preterm_rate_per100, fill = "Variable")) +
            geom_col(position = "dodge") +
            labs(
              x = NULL,
              y = "Rate per 100 Live Births",
              fill = "Maternal Age"
            ) +
            theme_minimal()

# let's make the same adjustments from last time 
## Change color & add bar border: color resource: https://r-charts.com/colors/
## bold text
age.raceeth.rates %>%
      filter(Variable == "MAGER.recode") %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = Value, y = preterm_rate_per100, fill = "Variable")) +
            geom_col(position = "dodge", color = "Black", linewidth = 0.8) + # adding border to the bars
            labs(
              x = NULL,
              y = "Rate per 100 Live Births",
              fill = "Maternal Age"
            ) +
            theme_minimal() +
            ylim(0, 30) + # change y-axis limits to range from 0 to 30
            theme(
                    axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
                    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
                  ) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = c("lightpink")) 

# Let's drop the legend, and flip the axis so that we can easily read the age groupings
age.raceeth.rates %>%
      filter(Variable == "MAGER.recode") %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = Value, y = preterm_rate_per100, fill = "Variable")) +
            geom_col(position = "dodge", color = "Black", linewidth = 0.8) + # adding border to the bars
            labs(
              x = NULL,
              y = "Rate per 100 Live Births",
              fill = "Maternal Age"
            ) +
            theme_minimal() +
            ylim(0, 30) + 
            theme(
                    axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
                    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
                    legend.position = "none" # drop legend
                  ) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = c("mediumpurple")) +
            coord_flip() + # flip axis'
            geom_text(
                aes(label = preterm_rate_per100),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
                hjust = -0.25,
                size = 4,
                fontface = "bold"
              )
```

```{r include = F}
### now make the facet of the two variables
age.raceeth.rates %>%
      ####--- removed the filter to age here ----####
      ggplot(aes(x = Value, y = preterm_rate_per100, fill = "Variable")) +
            geom_col(position = "dodge", color = "Black", linewidth = 0.8) + # adding border to the bars
            labs(
              x = NULL,
              y = "Rate per 100 Live Births") +
            theme_minimal() +
            ylim(0, 30) +
            theme(
                axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
                axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
                legend.position = "none" # drop legend
                  ) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = c("mediumpurple")) +
            coord_flip() + # flip axis'
            geom_text(
                aes(label = preterm_rate_per100),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
                hjust = -0.25,
                size = 4,
                fontface = "bold"
              ) +
            ####---- Adding the faceting here ----####
            facet_grid(Variable ~ .,
                       scales = "free_y", # removes the unused values
                       switch = "y",
                       labeller = labeller(
                         Variable = c(
                           MAGER.recode = "Maternal Age", 
                           MRACEHISP.fact = "Maternal Race & Ethnicity")
                       )
                       ) +
            theme(
              strip.placement = "outside",
              strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)
            )
```


## Preterm birth rates were highest for mothers with any diabetes and any hypertension history

The preterm birth rate was higher for mothers with any diabetes and any hypertension, with a rate `r hype.diab.rates %>% filter(Comorbidity == "DIAB.recode") %>% summarise(round(preterm_rate_per100[Reported == "Yes"]/preterm_rate_per100[Reported == "No"], 1)) %>% pull()` and `r hype.diab.rates %>% filter(Comorbidity == "HYPE.recode") %>% summarise(round(preterm_rate_per100[Reported == "Yes"]/preterm_rate_per100[Reported == "No"], 1)) %>% pull()` times the rate for no diabetes and no hypertension, respectively. 

```{r include = F}
## Alternative to facets. In my opinion, this works best when the variables share the same values so you can rely on one legend!

hype.diab.rates %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = Comorbidity, y = preterm_rate_per100, group = Reported, fill = Reported)) +
            geom_col(position = "dodge", color = "Black", linewidth = 0.8) + # adding border to the bars
            labs(
              x = NULL,
              y = "Rate per 100 Live Births"
            ) +
            theme_minimal() +
            ylim(0, 30) +
            theme(
                axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
                axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
                legend.position = "top" # drop legend
                  ) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = c("navyblue", "navyblue")) +
            geom_text(
                aes(label = preterm_rate_per100),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
                vjust = -1,
                size = 4,
                fontface = "bold"
              ) 


```

```{r fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, dpi=500, echo = F, warning = F}

            labs(
              title = "Figure 3. Preterm Birth Rate per 100 Live Births \nby Any Hypertension and Any Diabetes, U.S. Territories, 2020-2024", # add a title
              x = NULL,

            ) +
            theme_minimal() +

            theme(
                axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
                axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
                legend.position = "right" # move legend to the right
                  ) +
            scale_fill_manual(values = c("mediumpurple", "grey50")) + # change colors of bars
            geom_text(
                aes(label = preterm_rate_per100),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
                vjust = -1,
                size = 4,
                fontface = "bold"
              ) 
```

## Recommendations

The following recommendations have been identified from these findings:

```{r, echo = F, out.width = "55%"}
knitr::include_graphics("recommendations.png")
```


### (1) Continued research 
Continued analysis is needed to understand the unique drivers of higher preterm birth rates among certain maternal age and race and ethnicity categories in US Territories, which have distinct social and medical environments.

### (2) Community engagement
Working with community members to identify culturally relevant opportunities to address hypertension and diabetes.

### (3) Partnering with providers
Working with providers through territorial Perinatal Quality Collaboratives and other local collaborative organizations to identify culturally relevant opportunities to address hypertension and diabetes.

## Data Source and Methods

Data for the analysis was downloaded from the [CDC NCHS publicly available vital statistics birth data files](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data_access/vitalstatsonline.htm) for US Territories during 2020-2024. Consult the *User's Guide* files for more details on the data source. 

Preterm birth rates per calculated as the number of preterm births per 100 live births. Births were excluded if there was no information available on gestational age, based on the variable `OEGest_R3`. 

Age was categorized in 10-year age groups based on the `MAGER` variable. Any diabetes and any hypertension were categorized based on having reported either pre-pregnancy or gestational diabetes and hypertension, respectively. 

Additional details on the preparation of data for this report can be viewed in documentation available on our [GitHub page](https://github.com/Katie-Labgold).
